entries.title: LE scan start quota (5 starts per 30 s)

entries.title: Thermal status workload ladder
effects: limit FPS and bitrate to 90% at MODERATE and 80% at SEVERE while thermal reduction is on
entries.behaviour: With automatic cooling on, limit FPS and bitrate to 90% at MODERATE and 80% at SEVERE; stop streaming at CRITICAL or higher. Applies to every SoC family because the status is the platform's own ADPF signal; the thermal HAL defines when each status is reached.

sources.note: Statuses: LIGHT/MODERATE are 'some throttling, no significant performance impact'; SEVERE, CRITICAL, EMERGENCY, SHUTDOWN 'significant throttling that impacts performance'. getThermalHeadroom: 0.0 no throttling to 1.0 THERMAL_STATUS_SEVERE; the forecast is 'less accurate than using the current thermal status'. NaN means the API is unsupported or was called more than once per 10 s

The statuses come from the vendor thermal HAL: SEVERE is 'UX is largely impacted. Similar to 1.0 throttlingThreshold', CRITICAL 'Platform has done everything to reduce power'. Thresholds are vendor-defined, so the same status means different temperatures on different SoC families
getThermalHeadroom(int) is API 30+; addThermalStatusListener and getCurrentThermalStatus are API 29+

entries.fallback: No reduction (the selected FPS and bitrate run unchanged); the CRITICAL stop still applies
evidence: none: no benchmark run has exercised this phone-side condition; benchmark profiles set thermal_reduction=false
entries.confidence_note: Statuses and their meaning are official; the percentages are ours and were never measured on a throttled phone. The CRITICAL stop is not switched by this entry (platform safety).
legacy_switches: Settings automatic-cooling switch; DEBUG test_thermal_reduction=false (benchmark profiles)
entries.origin: ThermalGuardPolicy and MainActivity thermalStatusListener (kept; the 90/80% steps are our values)

entries.title: Smaller stream sender queue on low-RAM devices
effects: cap the stream sender queue at 4 MiB when isLowRamDevice()
entries.behaviour: When ActivityManager.isLowRamDevice() is true (Android Go and similar), a viewer whose queue passes 4 MiB is released to reconnect, instead of 8 MiB. The matcher cannot see RAM class, so the entry is universal and the effect applies only where the runtime flag is true.

sources.note: isLowRamDevice(): true on devices configured as low-RAM (Android Go edition builds); API 19+

entries.fallback: The original 8 MiB cap
evidence: none: no owned phone reports isLowRamDevice=true; MemoryThermalPolicyTest covers the selection
entries.confidence_note: The flag is official; 4 MiB is our choice: at 100-200 kbit/s it is minutes of video, far beyond any useful age. Unproven on a real Go phone.
entries.origin: BluetoothVideoSender MAX_QUEUED_BYTES (8 MiB) memory-safety release

entries.title: Release rebuildable state on onTrimMemory
effects: onTrimMemory drops rebuildable scan/route state; never stops a stream or call
entries.behaviour: At RUNNING_LOW/RUNNING_CRITICAL drop expired route suppressions; at BACKGROUND (40) or worse, while no stream, call or reconnect is active, also clear the scan-result maps (the next scan rebuilds them). UI_HIDDEN (every Home press) does nothing. Route failure counters are kept. Never stops a stream or call.

sources.note: onTrimMemory: RUNNING_LOW/RUNNING_CRITICAL mean the app is running and the system is short of memory; UI_HIDDEN and BACKGROUND/MODERATE/COMPLETE mean the UI is hidden or the process is cached; release resources that can be rebuilt

entries.fallback: No release (the maps are pruned by their normal freshness checks)
evidence: none: not exercised under real memory pressure; MemoryThermalPolicyTest covers the level mapping
entries.confidence_note: The maps are rebuilt by the next scan; their small size makes the saving modest. Android 14+ sends no RUNNING_* levels, so there only the BACKGROUND release applies.
entries.origin: new (the app had no onTrimMemory handler)

entries.title: Bounded private-call and group-relay control queues
effects: private-call control queue capped at 256, group-relay child control queue at 1024
entries.behaviour: Repeatable controls are bounded: one pending keyframe request per call (per child on a group relay), the newest display rotation replaces an older one, and at most 256 (call) / 1024 (group relay) keyed controls wait; a refused offer is logged. Hang-up, decline, cancel, stream-end ack, receiver-left and headers bypass the bound and are never dropped.

sources.note: A capacity bounds the queue; offer() returns false when it is full instead of growing without limit

entries.fallback: Unbounded queues (the previous behaviour)
evidence: none: legitimate use is one keyframe request or rotation per user action; MemoryThermalPolicyTest covers the bound
entries.confidence_note: The capacities are ours, far above legitimate use (keyed controls are at most 2 for a call). A refused keyed control equals a lost keyframe request or rotation, which repeat or are superseded.
entries.origin: AndroidPrivateVideoCall.controls and BluetoothVideoRelay receiverControls were unbounded LinkedBlockingQueues

entries.title: Act on the ADPF thermal-headroom forecast
effects: raise the workload ladder's status from the ADPF headroom forecast (never CRITICAL)
entries.behaviour: Proposed: treat getThermalHeadroom(10) above 0.85/0.95/1.0 as LIGHT/MODERATE/SEVERE for the workload ladder only (never CRITICAL, never a stream stop), sampled at most every 10 s, so reduction starts before the reported status rises. Documented guide thresholds, not locally tested.

sources.note: Statuses: LIGHT/MODERATE are 'some throttling, no significant performance impact'; SEVERE, CRITICAL, EMERGENCY, SHUTDOWN 'significant throttling that impacts performance'. getThermalHeadroom: 0.0 no throttling to 1.0 THERMAL_STATUS_SEVERE; the forecast is 'less accurate than using the current thermal status'. NaN means the API is unsupported or was called more than once per 10 s
getThermalHeadroom(int) is API 30+; addThermalStatusListener and getCurrentThermalStatus are API 29+

entries.fallback: The reported status alone drives the ladder
evidence: none: no benchmark run has exercised this phone-side condition; benchmark profiles set thermal_reduction=false
entries.confidence_note: The guide gives the thresholds for devices whose status lags and warns the forecast is less accurate; SoC families differ in forecast quality (vendor thermal HAL), and NaN is common on budget SoCs.
legacy_switches: DEBUG test_thermal_forecast=true enables the code path (default off)
entries.origin: new experiment; the app only logged the headroom at debug level

entries.title: Faster libaom preset while the phone is hot
effects: libaom cpu-used floor 8 at MODERATE and 10 at SEVERE
entries.behaviour: Proposed: while thermal reduction is on and the effective status is MODERATE/SEVERE, the software AV1 encoder's cpu-used floor is 8/10 and slower trial presets are blocked; the raised preset is not remembered.

sources.note: Statuses: LIGHT/MODERATE are 'some throttling, no significant performance impact'; SEVERE, CRITICAL, EMERGENCY, SHUTDOWN 'significant throttling that impacts performance'. getThermalHeadroom: 0.0 no throttling to 1.0 THERMAL_STATUS_SEVERE; the forecast is 'less accurate than using the current thermal status'. NaN means the API is unsupported or was called more than once per 10 s
AOME_SET_CPUUSED: real-time speeds 5..10, higher is faster (less CPU per frame); settable on a running encoder

entries.fallback: No floor (the governor's own overload stepping is unchanged)
evidence: none: no benchmark run has exercised this phone-side condition; benchmark profiles set thermal_reduction=false
entries.confidence_note: The knob is documented; its power/thermal benefit and quality cost were not measured on any phone.
legacy_switches: DEBUG test_thermal_speed_floor=true enables the code path (default off)
entries.origin: new experiment; NativeEncoderSpeedGovernor only reacted to measured encode time

entries.title: Battery temperature as the thermal signal on SoCs without a thermal HAL
effects: when the thermal HAL reports nothing, drive the ladder from battery temperature
entries.behaviour: Proposed, not implemented: if getCurrentThermalStatus stays NONE and getThermalHeadroom is NaN on a budget Unisoc/MediaTek phone, drive the ladder from ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED temperature (the app only shows it today). Matches the SoC families where a missing thermal HAL is most likely; reported only.

sources.note: 'If the initial value of GetThermalHeadroom() is NaN, the API is not available on the device'; the device model may not have the thermal hardware
ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED carries the battery temperature in tenths of a degree Celsius (API 5+)

entries.title: 16 KB page-size compatible native library
effects: libbluetooth_video_native.so linked with -z max-page-size=16384 and -z common-page-size=16384 (build time)
entries.behaviour: libbluetooth_video_native.so is linked with 16 KB max and common page size so every LOAD segment and the RELRO end are 16 KB aligned, and AGP stores it uncompressed and 16 KB zip-aligned. Build time; the flags are harmless on 4 KB devices, so the entry is universal and listed so the fact is in the one register.

sources.note: NDK r28 and higher compile 16 KB-aligned by default; AGP 8.5.1+ with uncompressed libraries gives 16 KB zip alignment; check zipalign -c -P 16 and that each LOAD segment is 2**14 or higher; the RELRO end must satisfy (VirtAddr + MemSiz) % 0x4000 == 0 or the library crashes on a 16 KB device; Play requires 16 KB support for apps targeting API 35+ from 2027-02-01

entries.fallback: NDK r28 defaults (LOAD segments aligned, RELRO end layout-dependent)
evidence: tools/check_apk_16kb.py and zipalign -c -P 16 on the built debug and release APKs (2026-10-10, NDK 28.2.13676358, AGP 8.13.0-rc01): LOAD align 0x4000 and RELRO end remainder 0 after the flag. The pre-fix debug library failed Google's documented RELRO check ((VirtAddr + MemSiz) % 0x4000 == 0, remainder 8192); release passed it. Whether a 16 KB device would have faulted on it was not tested
entries.confidence_note: Verified statically on the APKs; not run on a 16 KB device or emulator.
legacy_switches: build time: remove the target_link_options block in CMakeLists.txt

entries.title: libaom selects SIMD kernels at run time
effects: libaom: Armv8 NEON baseline, dotprod/i8mm/SVE only when AT_HWCAP reports them
entries.behaviour: libaom starts from the Armv8 NEON baseline and uses dotprod, i8mm, SVE or SVE2 kernels only when the kernel reports the CPU feature, so an older arm64 core never runs an unsupported instruction. The app's JNI file has no architecture-specific code.

sources.note: AArch64 NEON is a baseline (mandatory in Armv8.0-A); CRC32, dotprod, i8mm, SVE and SVE2 are enabled only when getauxval(AT_HWCAP/AT_HWCAP2) reports them (the __linux__ branch)
the NDK cpu-features library is used only when __ANDROID_API__ < 18; this app has minSdk 29, so getauxval is used
CONFIG_RUNTIME_CPU_DETECT defaults to 1 (runtime CPU detection)

entries.fallback: AOM_SIMD_CAPS / AOM_SIMD_CAPS_MASK environment variables force a feature set (debugging only)
evidence: generated aom_config.h of the arm64-v8a build (2026-10-10): CONFIG_RUNTIME_CPU_DETECT 1, HAVE_NEON 1, HAVE_NEON_DOTPROD/I8MM/SVE/SVE2 1 (compiled, hwcap-gated)
entries.confidence_note: From source and the generated config; no phone without dotprod/SVE ran the encoder.
legacy_switches: none at app level; AOM_SIMD_CAPS_MASK=0 in the process environment for debugging
entries.origin: audit of the shipped native libraries; no code changed

entries.title: Optional armeabi-v7a native library for 32-bit phones
effects: optional armeabi-v7a native library for 32-bit userspace phones (build time)
entries.behaviour: Proposed, build-time only: -PenableArmeabiV7a=true adds armeabi-v7a (libaom with NEON) so phones whose ABI list lacks arm64-v8a (32-bit userspace, for example some Android Go phones on budget Unisoc/MediaTek SoCs) can install. Reported on those SoC families as a prompt to decide; default off, shipped ABIs unchanged. Measured cost: release APK 10.7 -> 17.6 MB (+6.9 MB stored, about +2.6 MB compressed); speed on 32-bit devices unmeasured.

sources.note: armeabi-v7a is the 32-bit ARM ABI, arm64-v8a the 64-bit one; a device installs and loads native code only for an ABI the APK ships, picked in the device's preference order
Armv7 NEON is detected at run time from getauxval(AT_HWCAP) & HWCAP_NEON; without it the C paths run

entries.fallback: arm64-v8a only: a device without arm64 cannot install the app
evidence: none: no owned phone is 32-bit; size measured from an armeabi-v7a build on 2026-10-10
entries.confidence_note: Which budget phones are 32-bit is not derivable from SoC family alone (ABI list is the fact). Software AV1 on 32-bit cores is expected to be much slower; the speed governor then settles at cpu-used 10.
